observation: agent-loop-discipline routed 'known files/symbols' to rg in the same clause as literals and config/templates, while agent-loop-investigate in the same package forbade using text search to rediscover a PHP identity that map scope already resolves. tests/AdaptiveNavigationGuidanceTest.php asserted the wrong wording was present, so the contradiction was held in place by a passing regression test.

evidence.summary: Routed known files/symbols to rg together with literals and config/templates.
Same package, opposite rule: do not use text search to rediscover a PHP identity that scope already resolves.
assertStringContainsString(known files/symbols) pinned the defect; reverting the skill now fails 5 of 8 tests.
Records that #344 introduced the adaptive wording and that #342 still expected map scope for a known target, which is the overshoot this finding names.

hypothesis: A correction that removes an over-strong default can overshoot by one clause. #344 replaced Map-first ceremony with adaptive navigation and, while doing so, moved the one case that genuinely belonged to the semantic index onto the text-search side. The overshoot survived because the test written with it pinned the new wording verbatim rather than the distinction the wording was meant to encode.
validated_conclusion: When a guidance change reverses a default, check every case the old default covered correctly, and assert the distinction rather than the sentence. A test that pins exact prose from the change it accompanies cannot detect that the prose is wrong; it only detects that it changed. Two documents in one package that both route the same decision must be checked against each other, because the always-on one wins in practice.
